title: African Billionaires: Reshaping the Continent
script:
**NARRATION:**

In Lagos, a truck loaded with cement rumbles past gleaming towers—part of Aliko Dangote's $20 billion industrial empire that feeds and builds Africa. From a small trading firm to Africa's largest cement producer, Dangote proves that African solutions can dominate African markets.

Two thousand miles south, Patrice Motsepe descended into South Africa's gold mines as a young lawyer. Today, he controls a mining and energy empire, becoming the first Black African billionaire to sign the Giving Pledge.

The continent's wealth runs deep—just ask Nicky Oppenheimer, whose family transformed rough diamonds into a global luxury empire through De Beers, though controversy shadows the legacy.

In Nigeria, Mike Adenuga built his telecommunications network when skeptics said Africans couldn't afford mobile phones. Now millions connect through his towers.

These titans don't just accumulate wealth—they reimagine what's possible. From Dangote's refineries reducing fuel imports to Motsepe's renewable energy investments, they're betting billions that Africa's greatest fortunes lie not in extraction, but in transformation.

The narrative is changing. African billionaires aren't just joining the global economy—they're reshaping it.
